title: FactorIA assets.json
description: Per-asset import settings and provenance of a game project (the file assets.json at the project root, optional). Keys of `assets` are project-relative paths ("assets/hero.png"). The assets.* commands (assets.generate_image, assets.import, assets.set_import, assets.set_provenance...) write it; edit it by hand only for import settings. `factoria validate` checks it. Exports ship the import settings and drop the provenance.

defaults.description: Import settings every asset of a kind gets unless its own entry overrides them.

assets.description: One entry per asset, keyed by its project-relative path (forward slashes, e.g. "assets/music/theme.ogg").

import.description: Import settings of this asset: the texture keys for images, the audio keys for sounds. They override `defaults`.

analysis.description: Measurements the tools cache (loudness of a sound, image facts). Written by `assets.analyze_audio` and by exports; do not edit. A record only counts while `bytes` and `sha256` still describe the file, so editing the file never leaves a stale value in use.

loudnessLufs.description: Sounds: integrated loudness in LUFS (ITU-R BS.1770-4 / EBU R128) of the sound as it plays (a mono sound counts on both sides). -70 means nothing audible.

peakDb.description: Sounds: sample peak in dBFS (0 is full scale).

bytes.description: Size in bytes of the file the measurement describes (for a sound shipped as a QOA twin, the twin).

sha256.description: SHA-256 of that file in lowercase hex.

packed.description: Where `factoria export` packed this texture into an atlas (import setting `atlas`): the engine draws the texture from that rectangle of the atlas image. Written to the assets.json that ships in an export, never to the project's own file; do not edit.

atlas.description: Project-relative path of the atlas image ("assets/atlases/ui.png").

rect.description: Pixel rectangle of the texture in the atlas, without the padding around it: [x, y, width, height], origin at the top-left.

compression.description: GPU texture compression applied by `factoria export` (KTX2 with Basis Universal, transcoded at load time to BC7 on desktop and ASTC or ETC2 on mobile). auto: uastc for Android and iOS exports, none for desktop exports. none: ship the PNG. uastc: high quality, about 1 byte per pixel in GPU memory (4x less than RGBA8). etc1s: smaller files, lower quality (not for pixel art).

atlas.description: Name of an atlas group. `factoria export` packs every texture of the same group into one image, assets/atlases/<group>.png (fewer draw calls, and sprites of one group batch together); sprites keep referencing the original path. The atlas image is compressed like any texture, by its own entry in this file (the compression of the packed textures is not used). Only for textures drawn by Sprite (and so SpriteAnimator), ParticleEmitter and UI widgets: a Tilemap tileset or a mesh texture must not be in a group (`factoria validate` warns). Empty (default): not packed.

stream.description: Streamed sounds are decoded a little at a time while they play instead of all at once when loaded (a 3-minute track then keeps under 2 MB of decoded audio in memory instead of about 60 MB). auto: stream sounds longer than 10 seconds. always / never: force it.

normalize.description: Play the sound at targetLufs integrated loudness (ITU-R BS.1770), so tracks and effects from different sources sound equally loud. The loudness comes from the entry's `analysis`, which `assets.analyze_audio` and `factoria export` store; without a fresh one the desktop engine measures the sound when it loads it (mobile builds play it unchanged). The gain is at most 24 dB and never takes the sample peak past -1 dBFS.

targetLufs.description: Loudness (LUFS) that normalize aims at. -16 suits music and voice on any device; effects are often -18..-12.

convert.description: Conversion applied by `factoria export`. qoa: WAV files become QOA (lossy, about 5x smaller than 16-bit WAV, cheap to decode). none: ship the file as it is.

style.description: House style that assets.generate_image applies to every image, so generated art stays consistent.

prompt.description: Text appended to every image prompt, e.g. "16-bit pixel art, black outline, flat shading".

palette.description: Palette lock: generated images are reduced to these colours. Either a list of colours ("#rrggbb" or a colour name) or the path of an image whose pixels are the palette.

references.description: Project-relative images passed to the provider as style references with every image request (providers that accept them).

provenance.description: Where the asset came from. Required by store disclosures (Steam's AI-generated content survey) and credits.

origin.description: generated: made by an asset provider through the assets.generate_* commands. imported: brought in from a file (assets.import). original: made by hand for this game.

ai.description: Whether AI made the content. Always true for generated; set it for imported files made with AI elsewhere.

kind.description: What the asset is, written by the assets.generate_* commands, so the AI disclosure can tell sound effects, music and voice apart.

prompt.description: Prompt (or spoken text) the asset was generated from, style prompt included.

references.description: Reference images sent with the request.

seed.description: Seed, when the provider takes one.

license.description: License or terms of the asset ("CC0", "OpenAI terms: output owned by the user"...).

author.description: Person, studio or AI agent that made or chose the asset.

source.description: Where an imported asset came from: a URL or the original file path.

date.description: Date the asset was generated or imported (YYYY-MM-DD).

notes.description: Anything else (post-processing applied, edits made by hand).

recipe.description: How to make this asset again, byte for byte: the command that made it, its arguments and the project files it read. Written by the offline makers (assets.rasterize_svg, assets.animate_svg, assets.bake_sheet...); assets.regenerate re-runs it, and `factoria validate` warns when an input changed since (a stale asset). Provider-made assets have none: they cost money and would give a different picture.

command.description: The command that made the asset ("assets.animate_svg").

args.description: The arguments that make the same bytes again: paths project-relative, `seed` explicit, nothing that names this machine.

inputs.description: The project files the command read (an .anim.js module, an SVG, a prefab) with their hashes when the asset was made.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the file in lowercase hex.

sheet.description: Sprite-sheet layout of an image: a grid SpriteAnimator can play (columns, rows) and its named clips. Written by assets.slice_sheet, assets.animate_svg, assets.bake_sheet and the Aseprite importer.

frames.description: Number of frames used (row-major from the top-left); the last row may be partly empty.

padding.description: Transparent gutter in pixels around every cell (twice this between two cells): frame i's cell starts at x = padding + column * (frameWidth + 2 * padding), the same for y. Keeps filtered frames from bleeding into each other. 0 when absent.

pivot.description: Pivot of every frame, [x, y] in 0..1 of the frame from its top-left: the point that stays still. Sets Sprite.pivot when the sprite does not set its own. [0.5, 0.5] when absent.

clips.description: Named animations for SpriteAnimator (firstFrame, lastFrame, fps).

pivot.description: Pivot of this clip's frames; overrides the sheet's `pivot`.
